title: A sign that a row scrolls
question: Chip rows (the phone's calendar) and tabs (the admin panel's page tabs at a narrow window) are cut off at the edge with no sign there's more. One answer for both, on both sides, shown only where there's more to see. Which?

options.label: A: A soft fade
options.thesis: The row fades into the page at the edge that has more; nothing is added.
options.viewport: Calendar chips fading out at the right; Outreach's tabs fading at both edges part way along.
options.risk: Quietest: someone may still not think to swipe, and on a mouse there's nothing to click.

options.label: B: A fade with an arrow
options.thesis: The same fade plus a small round arrow on each side that has more; click or tap it to move along.
options.viewport: A › at the right of the calendar chips; ‹ and › on Outreach's tabs part way along.
options.risk: Adds a control to every row; on the phone it covers part of a chip.

options.label: C: A shadow at the edge
options.thesis: A soft shadow inside the edge that has more, as menus already show when they scroll; chips stay at full strength.
options.viewport: A shadow at the right edge of the calendar chips; at both edges of Outreach's tabs part way along.
options.risk: Easy to miss on the white page in light; nothing to click on a computer.
